title: Improve sensory contrast and ARIA for miniature visualizations and button pills
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As part of the compact density push, several miniature components (sparklines, micro-bars, compact legends) and the new button-pill component have regressed on perceived contrast and keyboard affordances. Some tokens used for tiny labels and disabled pills fall below AA thresholds at small sizes; microcharts are not exposing semantic ARIA roles or meaningful descriptions for screen reader users. Goal: remediate contrast failures, provide robust keyboard focus paths for pill/button groups, add ARIA semantics and announceable labels for micro visualizations, and produce a VPAT-ready evidence pack documenting tests and fixes.
acceptance_criteria: All affected components meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) for body text and 3:1 for large text where applicable; token map updated
Keyboard-only users can reach and operate every pill/button and microchart control; focus order deterministic and documented
Micro visualizations expose appropriate ARIA roles (img/graphics with aria-label or aria-describedby) and are testable with NVDA and VoiceOver
VPAT evidence pack created with screenshots, test steps, screen reader logs, and before/after token swatches
Design tokens committed with migration notes; components updated and E2E/axe checks added to CI
tasks: Run focused token contrast audit for compact token ramp (DESigner: Aisha) — audit report attached
Iterate button-pill visual and focus token in Figma; propose three fallback color ramps for high-contrast mode
Define ARIA/role mapping for microcharts (sparkline, microbar, dot trend) and write microchart accessibility spec
Implement CSS focus ring and update component JSX to include keyboard handlers and aria attributes (ENG-11744 referenced)
Add automated axe checks and a11y Cypress scenarios to the compact component storybook
Assemble VPAT evidence: screenshots, SR logs (NVDA/VO), keyboard walkthrough screen recordings, and an issues summary
